text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Spain grants Morocco a credit line of $40 million for small and medium-sized firms.
- Pro-government parties known as Wifaq take the lead with 367 seats in prefectoral and provincial assemblies.
- United Nations spokesman says a two-day meeting will be held in London starting July 19 between parties in the Western Sahara conflict, with Mauritania and Algeria attending as observers.
- Morocco's phosphates firm OCP reinforces its position as world leader through joint ventures and plans to submit to international auditing as part of its move to ensure quality.
- Belgian Foreign Minister Eric Dejricke backs one of his country's bus companies which seeks a deal to provide Casablanca transport firm with 400 buses.
